decisions.reason: As a close-to-core service that supports the firm's agency-focused differentiation, premium customer support is likely to meet or stay near aspiration levels, and the firm's growth and hiring give enough slack to retain it despite some uncertainty.

The software version management tool builds on existing technical capabilities and complements the hosting platform, so even if performance is mixed, management would likely keep it while using problemistic search to improve or reposition it rather than drop it immediately.

Because the data-processing-contract tool is distant from the firm's core offer, its results are more likely to fall below aspiration levels relative to core products, making it a natural candidate for resource reallocation toward hosting, support, and platform development.

Scalable hosting for agencies is close to the established business and explicitly presented as a flagship direction, so boundedly rational management in a growing firm would be very reluctant to remove it unless performance were clearly far below aspiration.
